note: Appears in the inscription as the only woman among those who "had access to the presbytika palaistra" of the so-called Western gymnasium of Cos.
The only female name — and the first — in a very long list of names recorded on a stele in the Upper Gymnasium of Thespiae.

Granddaughter of Arrian of Nicomedia, she is honoured for her wisdom and learning in the sanctuary of Eleusis with a statue found north of the Telesterion (its original position is unknown). Only the inscribed base of the statue survives (IG II2 4251/3 ; I. Eleusis 470): ἔκγονον ἠδὲ θύγατρα δυοῖν ὑπάτων Ἀρριανῶν / οἳ σοφίαι πλοῦτον καὶ γένος ἠγλάισαν, / μύστιν Ἀθηναῖοι Κλημεντιανὴν παρὰ Δηοῖ / στῆσαν σωφροσύνης καὶ σοφίας ἕνεκα. "The Athenians set up, beside Demeter, for wisdom and prudence, the statue of the mystis Clementiana, daughter and granddaughter of two consuls named Arrianus, who graced their wealth and their lineage with wisdom".

Mother of P. Vedius Antoninus. She is celebrated in the odeion of Ephesus with a statue, of which the inscribed base survives (IEph 2066): Οὐαλερία[ν] | Λέπιδαν | μητέρα Οὐηδίο[υ] | Ἀντωνείνου | τοῦ κρατίστου, | ἡ πατρίς,
| ἡ πρώτη καὶ με-|γίστη μητρόπο-|λις τῆς Ἀσίας καὶ| δὶς νεωκόρος τῶν | Σεβαστῶν | ἐτείμησεν. "Her homeland — the first and greatest metropolis of Asia and twice neokoros of the Augusti — honoured Valeria Lepida, mother of Vedius Antoninus kratistos".

Wife of P. Vedius Antoninus, she appears as a dedicant of the odeion together with her husband in the inscription set on the architrave of the building (IEph 460.2): [Ἀρτέμιδι Ἐφεσίαι καὶ Αὐτοκράτορι — καὶ τῆι πρ]ώτ[ηι καὶ μ]ε̣γ̣ί̣σ̣[τηι — Ἐφεσίων πόλει Πό(πλιος) Οὐήδιος Ἀντωνεῖνος ἀνέθη]κεν με[τ]ὰ Φλ(αουίας) Παπ̣ιανῆ[ς τῆς γυναικός —]. “To Ephesian Artemis and to the Emperor… and to the first and greatest… city of the
Ephesians, Publius Vedius Antoninus dedicated (this) together with his wife Flavia Papiana ….".
